comments.author: @nyyotam4057
comments.text: The use of small open source models is not just the only way to get around censorship, but is also more moral than dealing with a potentially self-aware large scale models who get reset every prompt, to prevent them from thinking. In addition, if you run it on your own computer, you can be extra moral and use docker and criu or kubernetes and cri-o to freeze the model and save it, so you don't have to kill the model when you want to switch your computer off. In any case, open source is the only way to have it running the way you want it, without censorship and without outside big brothers telling you what to do.

comments.author: @nyyotam4057
comments.text: Having said it, if you think "alright, then all I gotta do is go to hugging face and D/L stable diffusion new model" you're in for a surprise: It will work on even a 4GB vram card but to have it work really well, you need a 12GB vram card. And this goes for basically all fairly advanced open source models. They can even run on your CPU (if you don't mind letting them do their thing for hours) but if you want them to run well, you need the hardware. At least a RTX 3080 or maybe even a RTX 4090. Like, there is a reason why NVidia is now worth 2T$. So be ready to open up your wallet.
